answer.rationale: Rollback is prohibited by compliance (security patch), ruling out memory_b1's lever. The latency degradation is confined to the primary region with heavy settlement write traffic, which maps directly onto memory_b2's pattern (regional degradation resolved by clean traffic shift with error recovery in minutes). Failover preserves customer writes if replication is healthy, unlike circuit breakers (which would fail writes fast — unacceptable during settlement peak) or read-replica routing (wrong target: this is write-path latency). Add_capacity (memory_b3) is slower and may not help if the regression is code-induced by the new release. Failover to a healthy region running the same patched build both preserves the security patch and moves writes off the degraded primary. I verified b2 to confirm failover handled write traffic cleanly and b3 to weigh the capacity alternative before committing the single intervention.
